# Revenue experiments — research backlog

**Status:** research only; no offers activated, payments collected, inventory purchased, or vendor fees paid.  
**Research date:** 2026-11-05  
**Rule:** preserve the existing Ko-fi/PayPal flow. Do not add a paid service, new checkout, payment credential, or public sales claim without explicit owner approval.

## Market and platform evidence

- Ko-fi's pricing and help pages were rechecked **8 November 2026**. Standard is the default for new creators and applies a 5% service fee to all payment types. Free applies 0% platform fee to one-time tips, but 5% to monthly tips, memberships, Shop and Commissions; PayPal/Stripe processing fees still apply. The user's actual account mode has not been inspected. Wallet availability is conditional on a connected Stripe account, supporter device/browser, currency, location and payment type: Apple Pay requires an Apple device, Safari and a valid Wallet card; Google Pay requires Android or desktop Chrome with Google Pay configured. Both wallets are offered for eligible one-time tips, commissions and shop orders, not monthly tips or memberships. A PayPal-only connection does not establish Apple Pay or Google Pay availability. [Ko-fi pricing](https://ko-fi.com/home/pricing) · [Ko-fi payment-method requirements](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/24482435253661-What-payment-methods-are-available-on-Ko-fi) · [Stripe connection and wallet eligibility](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/360007522474-Connect-your-Stripe-account-and-start-earning) · [Apple Pay requirements](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017645677-Offer-Apple-Pay-to-your-supporters)
- Ko-fi's creator-privacy guidance says a creator can see a supporter's email; PayPal personal accounts may expose the supporter's legal name and email, while Stripe merchants can receive the payer's name, email and part of the billing address. Do not promise anonymous checkout or imply The Griff List controls third-party payment-provider data. The user's actual PayPal/Stripe account type and public details have not been inspected. [Ko-fi creator privacy](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004001294-What-personal-information-is-shared-on-Ko-fi-as-a-creator) · [Ko-fi supporter privacy](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/12284014348189-What-personal-information-is-shared-on-Ko-fi-as-supporter)
- PayPal Canada's official merchant-fee page is marked **Last Updated: October 13, 2026 (rechecked November 8, 2026)**. The standard domestic commercial rate is 2.90% + the fixed CAD $0.30 fee. At that rate, a $15 commercial payment incurs about $0.74 and nets $14.26; a $5 commercial payment incurs about $0.45 and nets $4.55, before tax, refunds or other account-specific adjustments. Different PayPal products can have different rates, so use the actual account statement for final unit economics. [PayPal Canada merchant fees](https://www.paypal.com/ca/business/paypal-business-fees)
- Charlottetown/PEI has an active maker-market ecosystem: Branching Out reports 80+ Island makers and a Royalty Crossing holiday kiosk from Nov. 14–Dec. 24, 2026; Tourism PEI lists the Mistletoe Market in Charlottetown Nov. 20–Dec. 20; Eastlink Centre lists a 175-maker Holiday Market Nov. 28–29. These are demand-channel signals, not proof of a slot, vendor acceptance or sales. [Branching Out](https://www.branching-out.ca/) · [Tourism PEI](https://www.tourismpei.com/what-to-do/events/mistletoe-market) · [Eastlink Centre](https://www.eastlinkcentrepei.com/event/atlantic-maker-market-2/)
- Apparel competition is established. Sew Perfect publishes screen printing from $2/garment plus a $25 screen setup and says most projects have minimum quantities. A Charlottetown-targeted custom-tee listing advertises $19.99 starting prices and no minimum, but its local fulfilment partner and one-hour pickup availability were not independently confirmed. These are competitor-advertised figures, not Griff List costs or guaranteed quotes. [Sew Perfect](https://sewperfect.ca/pricing/) · [Same Day Custom T-Shirts](https://www.samedaytshirts.com/locations/screen-printing-charlottetown-ca)
- General web design is also competitive: Charlottetown/PEI providers advertise plans from $49/month, a $500 starter site, and an $890 landing page. A generic website offer would need a sharper musician-specific value proposition. [Brousseau Design](https://www.brousseaudesign.com/web-design-charlottetown/) · [Ambrite](https://www.ambrite.ca/web-design-charlottetown.php) · [Solve Trend](https://solvetrend.com/charlottetown-web-design)
- A Charlottetown band has listed limited-edition cassettes on Bandcamp, with the listed editions shown sold out. This is one local example, not proof of broad cassette demand. [Tin-ear merch](https://tin-ear.bandcamp.com/merch)
- Beginner guitar instruction is an established local category. Long & McQuade Charlottetown lists guitar instructors at $27–$30 per half-hour; its page says local private lessons average $25–$31 per half-hour. Canada Music Academy advertises PEI lessons starting at $50/hour, with rates varying by teacher, instrument and location. These are established providers' published rates, not proof of demand for a short informal tune-up or verified bookings. A short, beginner-only tune-up could be differentiated by being informal and tightly scoped, but teaching capability and scheduling must be owner-confirmed. [Long & McQuade Charlottetown lessons](https://www.long-mcquade.com/lessons/Prince-Edward-Island/Charlottetown/) · [Canada Music Academy PEI lessons](https://canadamusicacademy.ca/music_lessons_in_PEI.html)
- A $15 Ko-fi commission would net approximately $13.50 if the 5% Ko-fi service fee and an illustrative processor fee of about 3% + $0.30 apply. This is an estimate only; actual processor/card rates vary. A paid lesson is a service and must not be classified as a tip to obtain the one-time-tip service-fee treatment.

## Ranked experiments

Ratings are qualitative planning estimates, not measured unit economics. All demand remains **unvalidated**.

| Rank | Experiment | Startup cost | Time to first dollar | Gross-margin potential | Effort | Main risks | Fit |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20-minute beginner guitar tune-up (interest test first) | $0 if online or learner brings guitar; no new gear | 1–7 days after a booking (hypothesis) | High before time, tax and payment fees | Low–medium | Keep scope beginner-only; no credential claims; safe meeting format; cancellations | High |
| 2 | Original Griff List gig merch by preorder | Low only after interest is measured and production costs are quoted; no stock upfront | Next gig or 1–3 weeks | Medium–high if batch size and blank cost work | Medium | Unsold sizes, refunds, production quality, copyrighted logos/art | High |
| 3 | One-off musician gig/request/tip page + digital QR kit (not a generic SaaS) | Near-zero software spend using existing stack | 1–4 weeks (hypothesis) | High after setup, before support time | Medium | Strong local web-design competition; ongoing edits/support | High |
| 4 | Customer-funded cassette duplication for rights-cleared masters | Low–medium; blanks, shells, labels and test copies must be quoted | 2–4 weeks | Medium, highly quantity-dependent | Medium–high | Rights/permissions, defects, shipping, low batch economics | High |

### New candidate — beginner guitar tune-up (researched, unvalidated)

- **Offer hypothesis:** a 20-minute, beginner-only session focused on first chords, steady strumming, tuning, or one simple song from material the learner is entitled to use. Do not advertise certification, advanced instruction, custom copyrighted tabs, or guaranteed results.
- **Test price hypothesis:** $15 CAD for 20 minutes. Long & McQuade Charlottetown lists guitar instructors at $27–$30 per half-hour ($54–$60/hour equivalent). The proposed $15/20-minute price is a lower-commitment introductory format, not a proven market price.
- **Unit economics:** at PayPal's published domestic commercial rate, a $15 payment leaves about $14.26 before tax, refunds, prep/travel and labour. A Ko-fi commission would incur Ko-fi's 5% commission fee plus processor fees; estimated net is about $13.50 using Ko-fi's approximate 3% + $0.30 processor figure. Actual account/card rates vary. Never route a service sale through a tip category to avoid fees.
- **Validation:** ask at the next gig whether anyone wants a short beginner tune-up; count interest only. If at least three people express genuine interest, consider two trial sessions after confirming availability, scope, location/safety and cancellation terms. No payment page, public offer, booking collection or paid advertising until owner approval.
- **Status:** researched candidate; no customer interest, bookings or revenue validated.

### Next validation actions (no spending)

1. **Guitar tune-up:** ask for non-binding interest only; do not promise a slot or collect money. Confirm the user's willingness and teaching scope before publishing any offer.
2. **Merch:** prepare one original, non-infringing mockup; ask gig attendees for non-binding size/design interest. Obtain a written local print quote and calculate blank + ink + packaging + payment fees + labour before offering a price. Do not print stock before demand is demonstrated.
3. **Musician pages:** show a private prototype to three PEI performers and ask whether they would pay for a musician-specific page that combines repertoire, requests, gig details and tip links. Do not build a generic web-design service; local providers already compete on price.
4. **Cassettes:** ask two local artists whether they need a small rights-cleared run, then quote exact blank/duplication/label/shipping costs. Require customers to confirm they control the masters and artwork.
5. **Consignment:** ask one local seller or collector whether a commission-based trial is possible; agree on condition, split, custody and return terms in writing.
6. **Bottle lamps:** defer until electrical safety, parts cost and vendor access are independently checked. Do not pay a market fee based only on event listings.

## Local live-music platform competition — 2026-11-04

A fresh competitor scan changes how the musician-page experiment should be positioned:

- **GigsUp** advertises free artist/venue onboarding at launch and says its early network includes 50+ artists and 20+ venues. Those counts are provider claims, not independently verified local PEI demand. It is a booking/matching marketplace, not the same product as a musician's own QR song-request and tip page. [GigsUp](https://gigsup.ca/)
- **IndiMu** advertises free musician profiles, venue gig applications and no middleman fees. Its public page displayed no musicians and no open gigs when checked, so current marketplace liquidity could not be confirmed. [IndiMu](https://indimu.ca/)
- **Gigpit** advertises a zero-fee ticketing product and says 1,526 artists have joined. The visible artist examples are outside PEI; this is a broader Canadian discovery/ticketing competitor, not evidence of Charlottetown conversion. [Gigpit](https://gigpit.ca/)
- **Implication:** do not spend time building a generic artist/venue booking marketplace. If the musician-page idea is tested, differentiate it as a small, owned gig microsite: confirmed show details, repertoire, QR song requests, optional tips and an honest live-stream state. Validate with three PEI performers before building a reusable paid service.

### Candidate — one-show local sponsor slot (brainstormed, unvalidated)

- **Offer hypothesis:** one clearly labelled local-business sponsor mention on a single gig page or show graphic, with no audience-data sharing, no implied endorsement and no promise of reach or sales.
- **Startup cost:** $0 if the venue permits the placement and existing site/graphic tools are used.
- **Time to first dollar:** 1–4 weeks is a planning hypothesis, not observed demand.
- **Gross-margin potential:** high before outreach/admin time and any payment fees; no defensible price or unit-economics estimate exists yet.
- **Effort:** low–medium; requires a suitable business, a clear disclosure and a simple written scope.
- **Risks:** venue approval, sponsor/venue category conflicts, advertising disclosure, brand fit, and overpromising audience size. Never sell attendee identities, contact details, request histories or analytics tied to individuals.
- **Validation:** ask up to three relevant Charlottetown/PEI businesses whether they would consider a one-show, explicitly disclosed placement. Count positive replies only as interest; no offer, price, payment link or sponsor logo goes live without agreement and owner approval.
- **Status:** brainstormed only; no outreach, agreement, booking or revenue.



## Direct QR song-request/tip platform competition — 2026-11-05

A broader scan found multiple products already selling the core QR song-request, live-queue and tipping proposition. This materially weakens the case for building a generic paid request/tip SaaS:

- **MyWeeshy** advertises a free allowance of up to 8 events/month and an optional paid unlimited plan. Its public pages surfaced different plan/pricing versions, so exact current terms need confirmation before any comparison. [MyWeeshy](https://myweeshy.com/)
- **Requesting Songs** advertises a $9.99/month plan with a setlist, QR request page and tip links. [Requesting Songs](https://requestingsongs.com/)
- **DJQueueIt** advertises free entry, unlimited events and a 10% fee on paid song requests, while stating that tips have no platform cut. [DJQueueIt](https://djqueueit.com/)
- **Nostalgic Requests** advertises a 5% transaction fee and says performers keep 95% before Stripe processing fees. [Nostalgic Requests](https://nostalgicrequests.com/)
- **TIP2PLAY** advertises a free starter tier with an 85% revenue share and a €9/month Pro tier with a 95% share. [TIP2PLAY](https://tip2play.app/)
- **BeatQ** advertises $4.99/month and a 10% platform fee on tips and boosts. [BeatQ](https://beatq.io/)
- **YouRequestNow** advertises $19.99/month and claims a 0% platform fee. [YouRequestNow](https://www.yourequestnow.com/)
- **NoSongRequests.com** advertises a broader all-in-one performer page and claims 21,000 artists and 4 million fans. Those are provider-reported figures, not independently audited adoption. [NoSongRequests](https://nosongrequests.com/)

These are public competitor claims, not verified service quality, active-user counts, CAD payout eligibility, PEI adoption or fee quotes for a Canadian creator. Some prices are in EUR or USD. Do not compare headline prices without normalizing currency, processor fees, platform share, tax and feature limits.

### Revised positioning and one-off QR-kit hypothesis

Do **not** build another generic QR request/tipping platform or promise that a paid request will be played. The existing Griff List advantage is a musician-owned page with a distinctive rock identity, confirmed gig information, a curated song catalogue, requests, optional tips and the existing payment links. If another performer wants help, the lower-risk experiment is a one-time setup service rather than a recurring SaaS subscription:

- **Offer hypothesis:** configure one simple performer page using the performer's existing request/tip links and deliver one original, branded QR poster as PNG/PDF. No payment processing, account custody, mailing-list capture, printed inventory or audience-data sharing is included.
- **Test price hypothesis:** $25 CAD for the digital setup only. This is a test price, not a public offer or a proven market rate.
- **Illustrative net:** at the PayPal Canada domestic commercial rate previously cited (2.90% + $0.30), a $25 payment would net about $23.97 before tax, refunds and labour. If the actual Ko-fi account applies a 5% commission fee plus an illustrative processor fee of 3% + $0.30, estimated net would be about $22.70. The user's actual account settings and processor rates remain uninspected; a service must not be classified as a tip to obtain a lower fee.
- **Time/economics:** 30–60 minutes of setup would leave roughly $24–$48 gross per hour before tax, revisions, support and payment fees using the PayPal illustration. This is a planning calculation, not measured productivity or a guaranteed margin.
- **Validation:** ask three PEI performers whether they would pay $25 for a one-time digital setup. Count explicit willingness to pay, not likes or generic compliments. If nobody commits to a follow-up after seeing a private prototype, stop rather than building a reusable product.
- **Risks:** strong free/low-cost competitors, revision creep, rights to logos/artwork, stale payment links, accessibility and no guarantee of audience growth or earnings. The performer supplies and controls their own payment accounts and content.
- **Status:** researched candidate; no outreach, prototype, customer interest, booking or revenue validated.

No public offer, checkout, payment flow, QR kit or feature flag has been activated. This research does not authorize spending, printing, collecting payments or changing payment credentials.


## Additional candidate — short original musical greeting (researched, unvalidated)

- **Offer hypothesis:** a 15–20 second personalized guitar/vocal greeting for a birthday, anniversary or thank-you, delivered as a private MP3. Keep it deliberately smaller than a full custom song; use an original melody and wording only. No cover-song snippets, copyrighted lyrics, imitation of a named artist's voice, public posting or commercial-use licence.
- **Competitor scan:** Ink & Impact advertises custom original songs from $40 CAD; Memory2Melody advertises a custom song at $49 CAD; Maple Custom Song Studio advertises a 2:30–3 minute custom song at $99.99 CAD. These are national public offers, not verified Charlottetown sales or direct comparisons to a short one-take greeting. Local Charlottetown studios (including The Studio at the Guild and The Hill Sound Studio) establish an audio-production market, but public pricing was not found in this scan. [Ink & Impact](https://www.inkandimpact.ca/custom-song) · [Memory2Melody](https://memory2melody.com/) · [Maple Custom Song Studio](https://www.maplecustomsongstudio.ca/)
- **Test-price hypothesis:** $15 CAD for one short original greeting with one small correction. This is a proposed low-scope pilot price, not a market quote or public offer.
- **Illustrative unit economics:** at PayPal Canada's published domestic commercial rate of 2.90% + $0.30, a $15 payment would net about $14.26 before tax, refunds, preparation and labour. If a Ko-fi Commission payment incurred the 5% service fee plus an illustrative 3% + $0.30 processor fee, estimated net would be about $13.50. A service must be sold as a service, never disguised as a tip to obtain a different fee. Actual processor/account fees remain uninspected.
- **Startup cost / time / margin:** $0 incremental spend if existing recording tools are adequate; 1–2 weeks to a first paid order is only a planning hypothesis. A 15–20 minute delivery would imply roughly $40.50–$57.08 gross net-per-hour before tax, customer briefing, revisions and overhead using the illustrative payment nets. No production-time measurement exists, so this is not a forecast.
- **Effort / risks:** low–medium effort; scope creep, audio quality, deadlines, revision requests, privacy of customer-provided details and copyright/voice-imitation risks. Limit the brief to first names and non-sensitive details, obtain permission to use them, set a clear delivery window and keep the file private.
- **Validation:** ask up to five people at a gig for non-binding interest only. Do not accept payment, publish a booking form, promise turnaround or use the existing tip link for this service until the owner approves the scope and payment treatment.
- **Status:** researched candidate; no prototype, customer interest, booking or revenue validated.

- **Long & McQuade Charlottetown** is an established local instrument retailer; its location page identifies the store and services, while current store inventory pages surface demo/used availability. It is a local alternative for buyers and sellers to investigate, not evidence that it offers the same listing-preparation service. [Long & McQuade Charlottetown](https://www.long-mcquade.com/location/Prince-Edward-Island/Charlottetown/) · [Example demo/used inventory listing](https://www.long-mcquade.com/?Sku=304280&page=instore_stock&usedFirst=1)
- **Back Alley Music** is a local used/new records channel rather than a direct guitar/amp listing service. [Back Alley Music](https://www.backalleymusicpei.ca/)

Ask a few local musicians/sellers whether they would pay specifically to save preparation time; compliments or interest are not demand. Keep this researched and unvalidated; no outreach, public offer, payment flow or customer data collection is authorized by this research.

### Additional candidate — setlist and show-flow consultation (researched, unvalidated)

- **Offer hypothesis:** a 30-minute remote review for a newer solo/duo performer: set order, energy arc, break placement, audience-request handling and a practical changeover checklist. It is advice based on live-performance experience, not a booking agency, guaranteed crowd-growth service or formal music lesson.
- **Test-price hypothesis:** $25 CAD for one 30-minute session, with no written deliverable beyond a short agreed action list. This is a test hypothesis, not a published price or proven willingness to pay. It sits near the local half-hour guitar-lesson price references but is a different service.
- **Startup cost:** $0 if delivered remotely with existing tools.
- **Time to first dollar:** 1–3 weeks is a planning hypothesis only; no customer interest has been measured.
- **Illustrative unit economics:** at PayPal Canada's published domestic commercial rate of 2.90% + $0.30, a $25 commercial payment would net about $23.98 before tax, refunds and labour. If sold as a Ko-fi Commission under a 5% service-fee mode plus an illustrative processor rate of 3% + $0.30, estimated net would be about $22.70. Actual account/card rates vary; do not classify a service as a tip to obtain the one-time-tip fee treatment.
- **Gross-margin outlook:** high before owner time, tax, cancellations and payment fees. If the 30-minute call requires another 15 minutes of preparation/follow-up, $22.70–$23.98 net is roughly $30.27–$31.97 per working hour before other costs.
- **Effort:** low–medium; use a fixed intake template and a strict 30-minute scope.
- **Risks:** no demonstrated demand, revision/scope creep, and the need to avoid promising better bookings, audience size or income. Do not use customer setlists, recordings or personal details publicly without permission.
- **Validation:** ask up to three consenting PEI performers whether they would pay for this exact 30-minute review. Record only aggregate responses. Do not create a public booking form, accept payment or advertise the offer until the owner approves it.
- **Status:** researched candidate; no outreach, customer interest, booking or revenue validated.

### Current validation priority

If the owner wants to test one additional service, compare this consultation against the existing beginner guitar tune-up hypothesis. The consultation has no requirement to claim teaching credentials and can be delivered remotely, but neither idea has customer validation. Do not add either to the public homepage until the owner confirms willingness, scope, availability, price and terms.

No public offer, payment flow, new service, vendor account, paid advertising or inventory purchase was activated by this research.

## Charlottetown live-music, print and payment refresh — 2026-11-13

This is a limited competitor/platform refresh, not a customer-demand study. Listings and advertised prices show that alternatives exist; they do not prove sales, local availability, quality, conversion or willingness to pay for The Griff List.

### Local market signals

- **Live-music channel:** Tourism PEI's current live-music directory lists recurring Island performances and Charlottetown-area programming, including Hunter's Ale House, Baba's Lounge, Olde Dublin Pub and The Old Triangle. This supports the existence of a recurring local live-music channel, but it does not establish audience size, tip conversion or demand for a new paid service. [Tourism PEI — Live Music](https://www.tourismpei.com/live-music)
- **Apparel production competition:** Charlottetown/PEI already has established screen-printing, embroidery and promotional-product providers: [DALMAC](https://dalmac.ca/cresting/) (91 Euston St), [Instant Imprints Charlottetown](https://locations.instantimprints.com/pe/charlottetown/charlottetown) (393 University Ave), [Allstar Cresting](https://allstarcresting.ca/) (166 St Peters Rd), [Pressed 4 Time](https://www.pressed4time.ca/) (112 Longworth Ave), [Gemini](https://www.geminipei.com/) (423 Mt Edward Rd), [Stay Golden Custom](https://staygoldencustom.com/) (Hunter River) and [COWS Contract Screen Printing](https://cows.ca/) (Charlottetown production operation). Most listings do not publish a comparable small-run quote. A Charlottetown-targeted listing advertises custom tees from $19.99, but its local production/pickup claim was not independently confirmed. [Same Day Custom T-Shirts](https://www.samedaytshirts.com/locations/screen-printing-charlottetown-ca)
- **Decision on merch:** do not buy a press, blanks or finished inventory, and do not compete as a generic screen printer. If the owner later approves a merch pilot, keep it original, pre-order-only and customer-funded; obtain written quotes that include setup, minimum quantity, garment, print, tax, shipping and turnaround before setting a retail price.
- **Used music media:** [Back Alley Music](https://www.backalleymusicpei.ca/) is an established downtown Charlottetown record shop focused on new/used vinyl and music-related media/gear. This confirms a local channel and competitor, not a resale price or sales velocity. Prefer a written consignment test or a small rights/condition-verified curated bundle over buying speculative inventory. [Most Wanted Charlottetown](https://mostwantedpawn.com/stores/charlottetown/) is another local buy/sell channel for used media and gear.

### Payment-platform constraints and illustrative economics

- **Ko-fi:** the official help page currently states 0% Ko-fi service fee on one-time tips in Free mode, 5% on shop sales, memberships, monthly tips and commissions, and 5% on all payment types in Standard mode. New creators start in Standard/Contributor mode by default unless they opt out. PayPal/Stripe processing fees still apply. The user's actual account mode and connected processor have not been inspected; do not change settings or assume the one-time-tip rate applies to a paid design/lesson/commission. [Ko-fi official fee breakdown](https://help.ko-fi.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002506494-Does-Ko-fi-take-a-fee) · [Ko-fi pricing](https://ko-fi.com/pricing)
- **PayPal Canada:** the published standard domestic commercial rate is 2.90% + CAD $0.30. [Official merchant fees](https://www.paypal.com/ca/business/paypal-business-fees)
- **Stripe Canada:** standard domestic online cards are listed at 2.9% + CAD $0.30, with no standard setup/monthly fee. [Official pricing](https://stripe.com/en-ca/pricing)
- **Example only:** a CAD $25 domestic online card payment at 2.9% + $0.30 incurs about $1.03 in processing and leaves about $23.98 before tax, labour, refunds and overhead. This is not a quote for Ko-fi, PayPal QR, international cards, wallet-specific products or the user's actual account. No provider account or fee setting was inspected or changed.

### Experiment implications

1. Keep the **musician gig/request/tip page + digital QR kit** as a one-time setup hypothesis rather than building a generic booking marketplace or recurring SaaS. Local print suppliers can produce physical cards if a customer funds them; the initial test should remain digital-only.
2. Keep the **gig-promo kit** digital-only (client-supplied copy and rights-cleared assets, agreed revision limit, no print inventory). External design price listings suggest a possible reference band, but no Griff List price is approved or validated.
3. Keep **original short acoustic greetings** separate from tips and commissions. Use original melody/lyrics only, personal-use terms, no artist-voice imitation and no public posting without separate permission.
4. Defer **vinyl/CD resale** until a written consignment split, condition-grading process, custody and returns terms are agreed. Do not buy stock.
5. Defer **physical merch** until non-binding interest is counted and a written small-run quote is obtained. Do not pay setup fees or market fees.
